q: An analyst wants to automate case assignment and endpoint isolation in one step. What should be separated first?
options: The case reference and evidence link into unrelated records
Routine preparation and consequential decision authority
The output of the inventory lookup and its timestamp
The live workflow and its recorded identity without any shared context
explanation: Preparation can be automated while a specific protective effect still needs authorisation.

q: Which statement best describes orchestration in a SOC workflow?
options: It coordinates information and work across steps or tools
It proves each connected system has completed its independent operation
It automatically transfers approval between operators on successive shifts
It is the same as the authorised effect of a defensive control
explanation: Orchestration describes coordination, whether its steps are manual or automated.

q: Which system should preserve the incident decision and its owner?
options: The event sender that originally generated an alert
The temporary cache that supplies a device's display name
The authentication library used by all connected service applications
The case system with references to supporting records
explanation: The case record is where investigators maintain decisions and ownership.

q: A timeout followed successful case creation. A retry arrives. What is the safest next check?
options: Create a second draft and delete whichever one has an older timestamp
Ask the alert provider to issue a new identifier for the same event
Find the existing effect by its stable key
Treat the timeout as a guaranteed cancellation of downstream changes
explanation: A lost acknowledgment leaves the effect uncertain until reconciled.

q: Which field distinguishes two receipts of the same intended intake?
options: The timestamp recorded by the retry attempting assignment
A stable source event identifier
The business owner copied onto the escalation note
The current severity label shown in the case view
explanation: The original source identity remains consistent across delivery attempts.

q: An internal directory is unavailable during intake. Which state is accurate?
options: Context unavailable; route the valid alert for review
No matching owner exists in the organisation's authoritative inventory
The alert is conclusively unrelated to any supported device
The case should be closed because enrichment did not finish
explanation: An unavailable lookup is different from a completed negative result.

q: What should the workflow contract define for malformed input?
options: A placeholder value that always makes it eligible for downstream effects
A reason to remove all associated case records immediately
The exact process for renewing protection on an unverified asset
The validation result and manual review route
explanation: Unexpected inputs should have a reviewable outcome without expanding authority.

q: Two legitimate observations name one device but have different source IDs. Why can both be retained?
options: Any case can only preserve one source identifier at a time
Different IDs prove the security events are unrelated across all sources
They are distinct events even if one case holds them
One event should be discarded whenever inventory recognises a device
explanation: Deduplication targets repeated intent, while case correlation handles related observations.

q: Which activity crosses an information boundary even though it changes no case state?
options: Reading the permitted internal case's summary in the work queue
Submitting a restricted identifier to a lookup service
Linking two existing evidence references within one approved case
Checking local syntax on a fictional sample without opening a connection
explanation: A read-only operation can still disclose information to another service.

q: An engine reports completion after producing an approval request. What should the shift note say?
options: Intake completed; decision and effect remain pending
Containment is verified because the workflow reached its final node
Approval automatically passed when the intake operation succeeded
The entire incident can close because the engine recorded a success state
explanation: Workflow completion and operational protection are separate states.

q: Why include the workflow revision alongside case effects?
options: To identify which device started the original observed event
To count every user who can view the case history
To prove the incident remained active until the next release
To reproduce which contract applied at the time
explanation: A revision lets reviewers trace changes in mapping and decision logic.

q: A stale alert is replayed days later. What should determine its effect?
options: The same action as the original alert under any policy
The dashboard's highest displayed severity regardless of received date
The contract's freshness rules and current case context
The elapsed time from the alert's subject appearing in the queue
explanation: Old observations can remain useful without justifying the same action now.

q: What is the main benefit of a reason code plus a case note?
options: Every run can report the same outcome to conceal sensitive facts
Counts can be grouped while preserving context for review
Analysts can stop recording source references when a situation is urgent
An owner can approve any operation without reading its scope
explanation: Structured reasons support metrics while contextual notes support decisions.

q: Which result best demonstrates repeat-safe case creation?
options: Two receipts return one verified case reference
Two execution IDs appear green in the engine dashboard
The repeat does not appear anywhere in the execution record
One case label applies to two separately created case objects
explanation: Repeat safety is proven by its effect, not the number of runs.

q: What is a suitable first automation candidate for a novice SOC team?
options: A broad production control change that varies by case
An anonymous approval channel for consequential actions
A public export of all case evidence to speed manual review
A narrow, tested internal inventory lookup
explanation: A well-defined, bounded repetitive task is easier to verify and govern.

q: The event record includes a free-form string naming a destination service. What should control the workflow destination?
options: Whichever destination the event text asks the workflow to use
The queue used by the last unrelated successful run
Its reviewed configuration and the source contract
The interpretation chosen by the employee whose device was named
explanation: Untrusted input is data and cannot grant routing authority.

q: What should a case reference provide to the workflow reviewer?
options: A permanent grant to operate every response service involved
A link to the corresponding decision and evidence record
A replacement for the source's actual event timestamp and identifier
A statement that all work associated with the alert is complete
explanation: Linked records let a reviewer reconstruct the evidence and state.

q: A lookup returns a device owner, but the source was not recently reviewed. How should the case use it?
options: Record it as contextual and request confirmation before consequential action
Promote the lookup to verified device control authority for all services
Discard the original evidence because the context is newer than the alert
Assume a lack of any owner whenever a lookup is older than the event
explanation: Source provenance and freshness help determine the context's appropriate weight.

q: What should persist if automated routing is paused for a repair?
options: Only previously confirmed effects and their display names
Nothing until an administrator can restart the service
An automatic permission grant for the delayed operations
Incoming evidence and the manual review state
explanation: A pause should preserve work and evidence for safe handling.

q: What action suits an unknown result of a consequential change?
options: Repeat it immediately until the engine reports success
Mark it failed solely because the client did not receive a receipt
Reconcile the effect through an approved source
Close the incident and record that protection must have succeeded
explanation: Uncertainty about the outcome needs reconciliation before another change.

q: Why name an owner for manual review states?
options: So all case outcomes use one generic label across environments
So unresolved work reaches someone authorised to resolve it
So the source service can remove records that require explanation
So pending events can automatically count as verified protection
explanation: Ownership makes a safe stop actionable rather than invisible.

q: A test input creates no case because it is outside approved scope. What is a successful result?
options: The input is accounted for with no unauthorised effect
There is a new case regardless because all inputs must succeed
The run enters the case list under the most recent valid event
The system drops it without a record so metrics stay unchanged
explanation: A no-action branch can be correct when the reason is visible.

q: Which evidence best proves an intended case draft exists?
options: An inventory response naming the same general business unit
The fact that an alert appeared in a source application's history
A renderer preview of the message the workflow planned to send
The owning case system's verified record
explanation: A verified downstream record demonstrates the effect where it occurs.

q: A workflow is judged faster after ambiguous cases were removed from its comparison. What should the owner do?
options: Publish the result immediately because average runtime is lower
Treat every removed case as a successful automatic routing
Compare eligible cohorts and preserve unresolved cases
Remove the comparison's date range and sample size to simplify it
explanation: Eligibility and unresolved cases affect interpretation of any reported improvement.

q: Which responsibility applies to each new workflow version?
options: Automatically inherit every permission ever held by earlier versions
Describe and test its expected branch outcomes
Delete records created by the old workflow so tests start cleanly
Ignore the recorded result as long as the configuration can be saved
explanation: Versioned expectations help reviewers check intended and unintended effects.
